hook: Strike a match and the head flares, smokes and leaves a black stub. The match is lighter afterward, yet not one atom has been destroyed. The atoms were rearranged into new substances, and some of them drifted away as gases. Every chemical equation you write in this unit is a record of that bookkeeping.

figure.caption: The parts of a balanced equation. Coefficients count particles (and moles); subscripts are part of each formula and never change. Each side holds the same atoms: 2 N and 6 H.

chain.cause: Bonds break in the reactants and new bonds form
chain.effect: the same atoms end up arranged into new substances

chain.cause: Atoms are rearranged, never created or destroyed
chain.effect: each kind of atom has the same count on both sides of the equation
the total mass before a reaction equals the total mass after, if nothing escapes

chain.cause: Subscripts say what each substance is

ideas: In a chemical reaction, bonds break and form so the atoms of the reactants end up in new substances, the products.
Evidence (a gas, a new solid, a color or temperature change) suggests a reaction; only a new substance proves one.
A balanced chemical equation has the same number of each kind of atom on both sides. Change coefficients, never subscripts.
Coefficients count particles and moles, not grams. Conservation of mass: total mass is unchanged when nothing can escape.

misconception.wrong: If the products weigh less than the reactants, matter was destroyed.
misconception.right: Matter is conserved in every reaction. A drop in measured mass means a product, usually a gas, left the container. Seal the container and the mass stays the same.

summary: A chemical reaction rearranges atoms into new substances. Because atoms are conserved, a balanced equation has the same atoms on both sides and the total mass does not change; balance with coefficients, which count particles and moles, never with subscripts.
